admission.definition: Executor decision that a proposal becomes a canonical fact through the temporal helpers. A verified claim's receipt must name an admitted use decision, recorded in verification.use_admission by verification.assert_admitted_use in the same transaction. Distinct from receipt outcome applied and from plan outcomes such as review_required or held.

alias.definition: A typed alternate name (synonym, acronym, former_name, handle, ticker, slug, misspelling, translation, model_alias). Unique per (entity, normalized alias, alias_kind), not globally unique across entities.

artifact.definition: Content-addressed stored object (sha256, bucket_class, storage_bucket, object_path) typed by artifact_type. Lineage edges record derived_from, supersedes, corrects, produced_by, consumed_by.

assertion-mapping.definition: content.unit_assertion_mapping declares how a unit kind's attributes become an assertion (a stream kind, relationship, event or attribute) with subject, value, qualifier and time templates. Deterministic mappings on first-party structured units take the cheap path; others carry a risk floor and go through Knowledge Services verification. evidence.extraction_record records which mapping interpreted which unit.

assurance.definition: How strongly a guidance item or vector item is backed. guidance.assurance_level is the vocabulary; retrieval filters accept a minimum assurance rank.

belief.definition: accepted, disputed, or unknown on a segment or occurrence. disputed does not replace an accepted current segment; the executor plans review_required.

canonical-entity.definition: One row in catalog.entity. kind picks the taxonomy.entity_kind whose attributes_schema validates the row's attributes jsonb. lifecycle is active, merged, or retired. Numbers that change over time are fact streams, never attributes.

census.definition: content.structure_census records what a captured representation structurally contains (headings, tables, lists, code, timecodes, speakers, figures, machine blocks) before any document kind or grammar is assigned. Kinds are open-world: a document_type can be candidate until its grammar settles, and promotion candidates come from census statistics.

claim.definition: An atomic statement with claim_type, status, and created_by_receipt_id. Facts may cite a claim as primary_claim_id. Subjects are attached via claim_subject roles subject, object, or context.

cost-class.definition: Catalog hint for statement_timeout and EXPLAIN gates. cheap and medium default to 15s; heavy is 60s and must not sequential-scan large relations.

digest.definition: content.document_digest is a structured digest of a document version (or a section/entity view) whose content.digest_item rows are records anchored to unit node ids — key points, entity roles, assertion references, changes, open questions, limitations, research directions. Prose summaries in content.document_summary render a digest; prose without a digest is not evidence.

domain.definition: A curated map of 5–20 relations that belong together (identity, temporal-facts, content, …). Default domain for a schema is schema_domains; a relation overlay may override it.

entity-kind.definition: taxonomy.entity_kind.code. Carries attributes_schema (validates catalog.entity.attributes), parent_kind (model version -> model; the link itself is a catalog.relationship) and is_work. catalog.entity.kind is a foreign key; unknown kinds cannot be inserted.

evidence-packet.definition: A retrieval-assembled bundle of members (verified claims, guidance items, source-faithful representations with scores and locators) for one question. Read with api.evidence_packet.

extent.definition: Source text for a date with precision (instant, day, month, quarter, year, relative, unknown) and optional earliest/latest bounds. Required when temporal_basis is explicit or carry_forward.

fetch.definition: acquisition.fetch is one attempt to obtain bytes from a URL — who (origin), with what tool, outcome, hash, spend — recorded before it becomes an evidence.source_capture. outcome unchanged means the same bytes as prior_capture_id, so no new document version; content.refresh_check records that per document.

fingerprint.definition: Digest of schema structure plus vocabularies, or of workspace plus enrichment. Artifacts also carry content sha256. Ingestion intents cite workspaceFingerprint; mismatch is WORKSPACE_STALE.

guidance-item.definition: guidance.item is one expert knowledge statement typed by guidance.item_kind (technical_problem, solution_pattern, failure_mode, compatibility_constraint, operational_practice, implementation_example, security_consideration, advanced_usage_pattern, setup_guide_step, research_direction) with a payload validated by that kind's schema, an assurance level, a provenance claim and the entities it is about (guidance.item_subject). Created only under a receipt.

head-revision.definition: authoring.work.head_revision_id, the current immutable authoring.work_revision of a course, module, lesson, activity, brief, report or dataset. Commands that change a work pass p_expected_head; a stale head is CONFLICT. api.works_authored lists works at their head.

hybrid-search.definition: api.search_unified fuses english full-text, trigram and (when an embedding is given) ANN channels with reciprocal rank fusion over the one stack, filtered by lens, tier, space, document kind, unit kind, entity, as-of and workspace. api.hybrid_knowledge_search_1536 is the older per-space-version entry.

idempotency-key.definition: Unique per tenant on operation_intent, knowledge_batch and authoring.command (product operations). A second submit of the same bytes returns the existing receipt or result; the same key with different input is CONFLICT.

identifier.definition: A schemed external identifier. scheme is a closed check-constraint vocabulary. Unique per tenant on (scheme, value), so one identifier names at most one entity.

intent.definition: A durable proposed operation. knowledge-read-intent.v1 and knowledge-ingestion-intent.v1 are the workspace contracts; the ledger row is orchestration.operation_intent with an idempotency_key.

knowledge-batch.definition: One committed admission transaction. commit_batch writes a knowledge_batch row with a receipt, idempotency key, and input digest, then advances the tenant head by one.

knowledge-continuum.definition: The four answer levels every question routes through. L1 catalog tables (api.models, api.software, …) filter, compare and rank without embeddings; L2 facts and time (api.changes_since, api.price_history, api.fact_locators, api.entity_at) answer what was true when and where it was read; L3 scoped semantic search (api.search_unified, api.talk_segments, api.document_units, api.document_digest) finds passages inside a scope; L4 is a budgeted agent loop over L1–L3 that files its result as a report.

knowledge-head.definition: Per-tenant monotonic sequence of sealed knowledge batches. Every snapshot and ingestion intent cites it; begin_batch fails rebase_required when the expected head does not match.

knowledge-time.definition: When a fact was admitted or closed. Stamped from the open batch. Current rows have k_to null; closed rows keep history. api.changes_since reports learned_at beside world_from.

lens.definition: Whose knowledge a row is. corpus is ingested industry knowledge (catalog, content, temporal, taxonomy, staging, acquisition, ranking, guidance, retrieval, the api catalog views); ours is what we author and learn (authoring, learning, access, library, inquiry, dataset, product, api.works_authored); private is one workspace's passages and conversations (RLS-isolated); evidence is claims, locators and admissions; machinery and legacy are runtime plumbing hidden from START_HERE and MAP. Every search-index entry and page carries a lens; retrieval.vector_item.lens and api.search_unified p_lenses use the same words.

locator.definition: A precise selection inside a capture (text_quote, table cell, media_timecode, page+bbox, JSON pointer, line range) with selected_content_sha256 and a normalized value. Support rows require a locator; api.fact_locators shows the locator, capture and typed unit behind a current fact.

logical-key.definition: unit_kind plus the values of the kind's logical_key_attributes (for a price_row offering|meter|tier|region), so the same unit can be matched across versions of a document. content.unit_change diffs versions by logical key; api.changes_since reports those diffs beside fact changes.

meter.definition: The thing an offering price is charged per (input_tokens, output_tokens, cached_input_tokens, batch_input_tokens, …). Required in the offering_price payload; with tier and region it forms the price series scope_key, and api.price_history takes it as p_meter.

mission.definition: orchestration.mission is the durable work envelope. Intents, artifacts and acquisition.fetch rows may record mission ids. Mission Control admission is out of band; this workspace only stores the id when supplied.

named-query.definition: An entry in the knowledge-query-catalog. Agents pass a name and params; they never send SQL. Build validation executes each example under the catalog role.

operation.definition: One `when '<op>' then` arm of product.dispatch_command / dispatch_read / dispatch_worker / dispatch_research_*, called through api.product_command(workspace, op, idempotency_key, expected_head, payload), api.product_read or api.product_worker. Each has a page under ops/ listing the relations the arm touches.

projection.definition: A derived retrieval object (search_projection, vector_item) pointing at a projection_target (entity card, guidance item, chunk, claim, summary, typed unit, digest, our authored revision or a private passage). retrieval.index_text_item is the one way a text becomes searchable; agents never write embeddings.

publication.definition: A published vector-space version that search is allowed to read. Unpublished or inactive versions raise insufficient_privilege.

rebase-required.definition: Transaction failure (SQLSTATE 40001) from begin_batch when expected head does not match the locked knowledge_head. Not a per-proposal outcome.

receipt.definition: Immutable orchestration.operation_receipt for one intent. Outcome is applied, rejected, noop, or partial. Facts and entities require a receipt id before they can be written.

relationship-kind.definition: taxonomy.relationship_kind.code with from_kinds, to_kinds, temporal flag, and property_schema. Trigger catalog.check_relationship_kinds rejects illegal endpoints.

release.definition: Two meanings. authoring.release freezes a root revision's closure for distribution (freeze_release, offer_release); a software release in the corpus is a library_release entity whose release_published event and version facts api.software_releases lists, and api.modules_affected_by_release connects the two.

rls.definition: Enabled on tenant tables. Typical policy km_tenant_access uses tenant_id = util.current_tenant_id(). Private-lens rows (library.passage, conversation.*) are additionally isolated per workspace; api.search_unified returns them only for the workspaces passed in.

role.definition: NOLOGIN Postgres roles. app_reader sees api views and RPCs. pipeline_agent selects bounded schemas. executor_service alone executes temporal helpers and writes catalog facts. Product operations run as authenticated (api.product_command / api.product_read) or service_role (api.product_worker).

scope-key.definition: Distinguishes parallel series on the same subject and stream kind (meter|tier|region for prices, episode for engagements). Default is the empty string. Part of the stream unique key; the database enforces no naming convention, so a correction must reuse the existing series key.

segment.definition: One assertion of a fact on a stream. Carries a world interval valid_during and a knowledge interval [k_from, k_to). Current means k_to is null.

source-tier.definition: A filter and a mild ranking boost, never a truth claim. T0 verified assertions, T1 our own content, T2 primary corpus (first party about itself, filers, registries), T3 third-party corpus, T4 live web. content.source_role.default_source_tier seeds it from who speaks; retrieval.vector_item.source_tier carries it; api.search_unified p_tiers filters on it.

staging-candidate.definition: An unresolved proposed identity. Not a staging copy of a fact. Resolution decisions are create, match, reject, or defer; vetting decisions are admit, reject, or defer.

stream.definition: The identity of a fact series, unique on (kind, subject entity or relationship, scope_key). Segments stack on a stream; overlapping current segments are forbidden.

stream-kind.definition: temporal.stream_kind.code with subject_mode, subject_kinds, status_values, unit_values, requires_amount, and payload_schema. commit_batch validates slot rules. offering_price is the one home for prices (payload meter|tier|region), benchmark_score the one home for benchmark numbers.

support.definition: A k-stamped link from a claim and locator to a segment or event occurrence. Written only through temporal.admit_support inside an open batch.

task.definition: A question family with navigation, a read or ingestion operation, expected shape, and pitfalls. The shortest path from a natural-language question to a valid catalog query, product operation or intent.

temporal-basis.definition: Why the world interval is believed. explicit and carry_forward require an extent; observation_bounded is “true at capture time”; unresolved is an admitted gap.

tenant.definition: Isolation key read from GUC app.tenant_id by util.current_tenant_id(). Missing context fails closed. RLS policies compare tenant_id to that function.

two-clocks.definition: World time and knowledge time together. entity.at(entity, T, K) answers what was true at T as we knew it at K; price_history shows every belief with both clocks.

typed-unit.definition: A content.document_node with a unit_kind from the content.unit_kind grammar (price_row, transcript_segment, release_entry, table_row, slide, section, …), attributes validated by that kind's JSON Schema, a logical_key stable across captures and a typed position (offsets, page, bbox, timecodes). Units are the anchors for locators, entity roles, extraction records and retrieval items; chunks are derived from units, never the other way round.

vector-space.definition: A named retrieval space (units, digests, entity_cards, assertions, own_content, learner_notes, knowledge_text, …) with versions and publications. api.search_unified takes space slugs as a facet; agents read only published versions.

verification-run.definition: A knowledge_verification component run that must be sealed before cited claims may be materialized; the database records the admitted use in verification.use_admission and a verified claim names an admission-bound receipt.

vocabulary.definition: Allowlisted code tables such as taxonomy.entity_kind, taxonomy.relationship_kind, temporal.stream_kind, content.document_type, content.unit_kind, content.format, content.source_role and guidance.item_kind. Slot rules and endpoint kinds are enforced at write time.

work.definition: catalog.work is the bibliographic row behind an entity whose kind is a work (paper, talk, media work, story, case study; taxonomy.entity_kind.is_work). Its content lives in content.document rows that point back through work_entity_id.

workspace.definition: Generated projection of schema-ir.v1 into Markdown layers, search indexes, operation pages and the named-query catalog. Agents search then read a domain or task page; they never read schema-ir.json whole. Not to be confused with authoring.workspace, the product's team container.

world-time.definition: When the world was like this. Stored as a tstzrange bounded below with [) bounds. Distinct from when we came to know it.
